title: Sessions from 1990s: Lorber, Hancock, Lainie Kazan, Pat Williams
summary: Brown reads through later credits and Laws remembers some, such as Lainie Kazan and Pat Williams's Sinatraland.

blocks.x: You were on one tune called Obsession on this cut, and Milton Nascimento sang with her on this. I have this at home. So I remember this. Mean Lean. So we can trace it from it’s very first recording, back on Atlantic, through to In the Beginning, where it shows up as the closing, and then now – so every decade there seems to be another version.
We talked about that yesterday too. Here’s that sideman date with Jeff Lorber. Then Herbie, This is the Drum.

Yeah, but that was – that’s one of the ones I think that kind of skirted out underneath the wire for most people, because Herbie was really doing Rocket and all that kind of stuff. It was another period for Herbie. Then a couple ones with Harvey Mason – one session with Harvey. Then Lainie Kazan, Body and Soul.

She told me I did – I saw her at the Skirball. She walked up to me, say, “I’m Lainie Kazan.” I didn’t remember who’s that. Then she said, “You recorded with me.” So I got a copy of it. Lainie Kazan, yeah. Then I listened to it, actually, after that.
Diane Reeves, Harvey Mason again, Joe Sample – dapper Joe.
Yeah, Joe did – he did a retake on, I think, It Happens Every Day.

It Happens Every Day, yeah. Michael Martin. I’m not familiar with him. Then some more with Don Sebesky. It looks like RCA Victor, a couple things. Dave Samuels, Larry Coryell, Eddie Gomez, Marty Morrell. Then Pat Williams, Sinatraland.
Yeah, I just did that recently. That’s about – that’s last year.
This one is – the actual sessions of this is ’97.

Oh, well now, I did something recently with Pat Williams, right down the street at Capitol Records. I got the music on my stand in my office right now. It sounds like it was Sinatraland or something like.
Maybe he did another – resurrect that one.
Oh, yeah, I remember that now, because Eddie Daniel’s on there, isn’t he?
